text: Qua tempestate praesides procurabant, vir quidam a Bethlehema Judaeae, orta in finibus illis fame, profectus est ad peregrinandum in agrum Moabiticum, una cum sua conjuge, duobusque filiis.
note: proofread: comma for 1738's semicolon after *Jūdææ*: it cuts the subject *vir quīdam* from its verb *profectus est*, the ablative absolute *ortā … famē* standing between, so commas bracket it (as the 1:18 row's colon before the main verb made a comma, Judg 1:4, 2:10; Wikisource prints a comma here); *Mōabīticum* capital kept, as the current row (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Viri nomen erat Elimelechus, mulieris Noemis: duorum filiorum Mahalon et Chelion, Ephrataei, ex Bethlehema Judaeae. His in agrum Moabiticum profectis, ibique degentibus,
note: *Mōabīticum* capital, as 1:1 (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: quum apud Moabitas agens audivisset, Jovam suis subvenisse, eisque annonam levasse,
note: no paragraph: the verse continues the period begun at 1:5 *Mulier autem … superstes, cum … audīsset, … contendit, eāsque … admonuit* (1738 runs on, *superstes, quum*); the BSB's heading falls inside it and the sentence starts mid-verse, so no paragraph is placed, as Judg 19:29 (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: easque in itinere sic admonuit: “Revertimini utraque in suae matris domum: rependat vobis Jova pietatem, qua tum erga mortuos tum erga me usae estis.
note: Naomi's words are direct (imperative *Revertiminī*, *vōbīs*), opened after 1738's colon and closed at 1:9 *nancīscāminī*; capital at the speech's start (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Faxit Jova, ut quietem suum utraque apud maritum nanciscamini.” Haec quum locuta, eas deoscularetur, illae in lacrimas erumpentes,
note: Naomi's speech closes at *nancīscāminī*; the narrative resumes; 1:10 (*affirmābant, sēsē … esse reversūrās*) is reported, unmarked, where the BSB quotes (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Sed Noemis eas ita hortata est: “Revertimini, meae filiolae, cur me comitemini? Numquid ego adhuc in utero gesto filios, qui vobis futuri sint viri?
note: paragraph: 1:1–13 would be about 270 words (decision 52); the BSB breaks here, and Naomi's second plea begins a sentence at the verse start; direct, opened here and closed at 1:13; the vocative *meæ fīliolæ* set off by commas (1738 none), as Deuteronomy's rule (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Revertimini, meae filiolae, discedite: nam ego quidem grandior sum, quam ut sim apta viro. Quod si maxime spem esse putarem, viroque vel in proximam noctem tradita, filios gignerem:
note: inside Naomi's speech; the vocative set off by commas, as 1:11 (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: an estis exspectaturae, donec adoleverint, et tamdiu sine viris duraturae? Non ita, meae filiae. Equidem valde vestra caussa doleo; sed me Jovae manus urget.”
note: Naomi's speech (1:11–13) closes at *urget* (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Tum illae ploratum integrant, et Orpha socrum suam osculata, ei valedicit. At Rutha cum ea haerebat,
note: paragraph: the parting (the BSB breaks here); 1738 indents within the verse, at *At Rutha* (text/orig/RUT.usfm), but that sentence runs on into 1:15, so the paragraph stands at the verse start, where *Tum illæ* begins a sentence (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: et Noemis sic eam adlocuta est: “Vides, ut tua fratria repetat patrios penates: revertere una cum fratria.”
note: Naomi's words direct (*Vidēs … revertere*), after 1738's colon; capital at the speech's start (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: At Rutha: \\q1 “Ne me urge,” inquit, “ut te relinquam, \\q2 atque a te discedam: \\q1 nam quo tu cumque ibis, ego ibo: \\q2 ubi tu diversaberis, ego diversabor: \\q1 communis mihi tecum erit populus, \\q2 communis Deus.
note: Ruth's vow (1:16–17) as poetry on the BSB's lines (it sets 1:16b–17 as verse): Castellio keeps the Hebrew's paired members clause for clause, his colons marking the halves (*quō tū … ego ībō: ubi tū … ego dīversābor*), and the elliptic *commūnis Deus*, so verse-like (Judges' and Deuteronomy's rule); mid-verse after *At Rūtha:*, as 1 Cor 1:19; *inquit* set off by commas, the quotation closed and reopened (decision 65) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Ubi tu morieris, ego moriar, \\q2 ibique sepeliar: \\q1 atque ita mihi sit Jova propitius, \\q2 ut una me mors a te divellet.”
note: the vow's last four lines, as the BSB's; the speech closes here (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Tum illa videns, eam secum obstinavisse proficisci, dissuadere desiit.
note: paragraph: prose after the poetry, and 1738 itself indents here (text/orig/RUT.usfm); the colon before the main verb *dēsiit* made a comma, as Judg 1:4, 2:10 (1738 *proficisci: dissuadere*) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: dicebat: “Nolite me Noemim vocare, vocate me Maram: nam ingenti moerore me adfecit Omnipotens.
note: Naomi's words direct (*Nōlīte mē … vocāte mē*), 1:20–21, after 1738's colon; the women's question at 1:19 is reported (*num ea Nœmis esset*), unmarked; *Omnipotēns* capital, God's title used alone (Shaddai, the BSB's "the Almighty"), as the settled Gen 49:25 *ab Omnipotente* (1738 *omnipotens*); the BSB sets no poetry here (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Quum plena discesserim, inanem Jova reduxit: cur me Noemim adpellatis, quam rerum praepotens Jova malo adflixerit?”
note: Naomi's speech closes here; *præpotēns* stays lower case, an adjective with *Jōva* (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Igitur reversae Noemis et Rutha Moabitis, nurus ejus, ex agro Moabitico, Bethlehemam initio messis hordeorum venerunt.
note: *Mōabīticō* capital, as 1:1 (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Et Rutha Moabitis a Noemi copiam petivit eundi rus, et spicas colligendi post quemvis, si quem nancisceretur, qui id ei beneficii concederet. Atque illa ei ita dixit: “I sane, mea filia.”
note: Ruth's request is reported (*cōpiam petīvit eundī … sī quem nancīscerētur*), unmarked though the BSB quotes it; Naomi's answer direct (*Ī sānē*), capital at the speech's start (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Ita rus profecta Rutha, coepit post messores spicilegium facere: acciditque, ut fundus ille esset Boozi, gentilis Elimelechi.
note: paragraph: Ruth goes to the field; 1738 indents here (text/orig/RUT.usfm), and the BSB breaks (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Atque is Boozus tum Bethlehema adveniens, sic messores salutavit: “Adsit vobis Jova.” Cui illi: “Et tibi faveat Jova.”
note: paragraph: Boaz arrives, a new scene (2:4–7); 1738 indents here, the BSB breaks; the greeting and the reply direct, after 1738's colons, capitals at each speech's start (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Et Boozus famulum suum curatorem messis adloquens: “Cuja est ista puella?” inquit.
note: Boaz's question direct; *inquit* after it outside the marks (as the settled *“Scīsne Græcē?” inquit.*) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Cui ille: “Puella est Moabitis, quae remigrantem ex agro Moabitico Noemim comitata est.
note: the foreman's answer direct, opened here and closed at 2:7; *Mōabīticō* capital, as 1:1 (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Rogavit autem, ut sibi liceret apud manipulos spicilegium facere post messores, mansitque hic hactenus, ex quo mane venit: tam paullum manet domi.”
note: still the foreman (*hīc*, *manet*); Ruth's request inside it is reported (*ut sibi licēret*), so no ‘…’ where the BSB has one; closed at *domī* (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Tum Boozus ad Rutham: “Audin', filia? Ne iveris in alium agrum ad legendum spicas, neque hinc discesseris; sed hic haereto apud meas operarias,
note: proofread: capital *Nē* after the question mark: *Audīn', fīlia?* is a whole question and the prohibition starts a new sentence (as 1:11 *comitēminī? Numquid*); 1738 lower case, its habit after any question mark; otherwise the current row (paragraph, the vocative set off, quotation open to 2:9) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: et videto, ut eas sequaris, quo in agro metent. Ego operariis vetabo, ne sint tibi molesti. Quod si sities, petes potum ex iisdem vasis, quibus hauriunt ipsi.”
note: Boaz's speech closes here (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Tum illa in faciem procumbens, et honorem illi submisse praebens, ita dixit: “Quid est, ut tu me peregrinam adficias eo beneficio, ut mei rationem habeas?”
note: Ruth's question direct, after 1738's colon (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Cui Boozus respondens: “Narratum est mihi,” inquit, “qualem tu te praestiteris erga socrum tuam, post obitum viri tui: utque relicto utroque parente terraque patria, te ad populum tibi antea ignotum contuleris:
note: Boaz's answer direct, 2:11–12; *inquit* set off by commas, the quotation closed and reopened (decision 65) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: quod factum Jova tibi Deus Israelitarum cumulatissimo praemio rependet, sub cujus alarum praesidium tu te receperis.”
note: Boaz's speech closes here (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Et illa: “Agnosco tuam erga me benignitatem, domine, qui tam humana oratione confirmes animum meum consolando; quum tamen indigna sim, quae vel in ancillarum tuarum numerum veniam.”
note: Ruth's answer direct; *domine* lower case, addressed to Boaz, a man (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Deinde sub horam capiendi cibi, jussit eam Boozus accedere, et pane vesci, buccellasque suas in aceto intingere: quumque illa messorum lateri adsedisset, porrexit ei polentam. Illa ubi cibum ad satietatem cepit, quum ex eo superfuisset,
note: paragraph: mealtime (the BSB breaks here); 1738 indents within the verse at *Illa ubi*, but that sentence runs on into 2:15, so the paragraph stands at the verse start, where *Deinde* begins a sentence; Boaz's invitation is reported (*jussit eam … accēdere*), unmarked, and so are his orders at 2:15–16 (*præcēpit, nōn modo nē … prohibērent*) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Ita illa spicas in agro legit ad vesperum, trituratumque, quod legerat (fuit autem circiter ephi hordei),
note: proofread: no comma before the parenthesis, the comma that closes the relative *quod lēgerat* moved after it, before the main verb *in oppidum intulit* (2:18); 1738 *legerat, (fuit … hordei)*, Wikisource *quod legerat (fuit … hordei) in oppidum*; paragraph kept as the current row (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Et socrus: “Ubi hodie collegisti?” inquit, “aut ubi operata es? Bene precor illi, qui tui rationem habuit.” Tum illa socrui exponit, quo pacto apud illum operata fuisset: docetque, viro illi, apud quem eo die operata sit, nomen esse Boozus.
note: Naomi's questions direct; *inquit* set off by commas, the colon after it a comma, the quotation closed and reopened (decision 65); Ruth's answer reported (*expōnit, quō pactō … docetque … nōmen esse*), unmarked where the BSB quotes (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Et Noemis: “Precor illi Jovam propitium, qui suam beneficentiam neque a vivis avertit, neque a mortuis. Is quidem propinquus est nobis,” inquit, “et nostrae consanguinitatis.”
note: Naomi's words direct, *inquit* set off (decision 65); one speech, as Castellio gives it with one *inquit* inside (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Et Rutha: “Quin etiam me monuit,” inquit, “ut apud suos operarios haererem, usque ad peractam omnem suam messem.”
note: Ruth's words direct; Boaz's order inside them reported (*ut … hærērem*), so no ‘…’ where the BSB has one (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Cui socrus: “Et sane praestat,” inquit, “filia, ut ejus operarias sequare, ne in alio fundo prohibearis.”
note: Naomi's words direct, *inquit* set off (decision 65) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Interea dum apud socrum manet, Noemis cum ea sic locuta est: “Requiem tibi, mea filia, volo quaerere, ut bene sit tibi.
note: Naomi's words, direct (3:1–4, *sīc locūta est:*), opened after 1738's colon with a capital, as Judges (*Et illa: “Equidem…*, Judg 4:9); the draft's \\p (the BSB's heading) kept (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Quumque discedet cubitum, observato locum, in quo cubabit, eumque adito, et, detectis ejus pedibus, cubato. Ipse tibi, quid facto sit opus, ostendet.”
note: Naomi's speech closed (as the BSB, 3:4); the colon between the *cum* clause and its main verb *observātō* a comma for clarity, as Judges' readers did before a main verb (Judg 1:4) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Et illa: “Quidquid tu mihi mandas, exsequar.”
note: Ruth's answer, direct; *Et illa:* keeps 1738's colon (no *inquit*), as the settled Judges' *Et illa: “Equidem…*; no paragraph per speaker (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Haec locuta descendit ad aream, et omne socrus mandatum exsecuta est.
note: paragraph: a new scene (she goes down to the threshing floor); 1738 indents here (text/orig/RUT.usfm, \\p before 3:6); 3:1–18 is 326 words in one paragraph otherwise (decision 52): 88, 192 and 46 after 3:6 and 3:16 (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: inquit: “Quae tu es?” Cui illa, “Ego sum Rutha,” inquit, “ancilla tua, quae peto, ut tu in me gremium tuum exporrigas: nam propinquus es.”
note: Boaz's question and Ruth's answer, direct; *inquit* set off by commas, the quotation closed and reopened (decision 65): *Cui illa:* becomes *Cui illa,* before the first words, as the settled Judges' *Cui ille, “Pergimus,” inquit,* (1738 *Cui illa: ego sum Rutha, inquit,*); speech openings capital; 1738 runs 3:9 on (the draft's line break inside the verse goes) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Et Boozus, “Jovam tibi, filia, opto propitium,” inquit, “tu priorem pietatem hac posteriore superasti, quae juvenes sive pauperes sive divites secuta non sis.
note: Boaz's speech, direct (3:10–13, as the BSB); *inquit* set off by commas (decision 65), as the settled Judg 6:23 *At Jōva, “Salvus es,” inquit, “dēpōne metum* where 1738 prints *At Ioua: saluus es, inquit: depone*; the speech runs on to 3:13 (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Quamobrem bono es animo, filia: quidquid postulas, tibi faciam: scit enim cuncta meorum popularium civitas, te mulierem esse virtute praeditam.

text: Quiesce hac nocte. Mane si te ille propinquitatis jure ducere voluerit; bene est, ducat sane: sin autem noluerit; ego per Jovam immortalem ducam: quiesce in matutinum.”
note: Boaz's speech closed (as the BSB); 1738's semicolons kept; the draft's line break inside the verse goes (1738 runs on) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Igitur illa ad ejus pedes in matutinum quievit, surrexitque, antequam posset quis alterum agnoscere: et ille ei praecepit, ut caveret, ne, in aream venisse mulierem, rescisceretur:
note: proofread: paragraph: the threshing-floor dialogue (3:9–13) ends and the narrative resumes at dawn; 1738 indents here (text/orig/RUT.usfm, \\p before 3:14) and the BSB breaks here too (marks b m); a narrative break, not one per speaker (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Illa in oppidum ad socrum venit: quaerentique, quid egisset, exposuit omnia, quae sibi fecisset homo,
note: paragraph: a new scene (Ruth back with Naomi); the BSB and 1738 both break here. 3:16–17 stay unquoted: Naomi's question and Ruth's account, Boaz's words with it, are reported (*quærentīque, quid ēgisset, exposuit … utque … dedisset, negāns, vacuæ veniendum esse*), though the BSB quotes them (decisions 4, 25) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Tum socrus, “Exspecta,” inquit, “filia, donec videas, quo cadat res. Nam homo numquam hodie, nisi re perfecta, conquiescet.”
note: Naomi's words, direct, *inquit* set off by commas (decision 65), as 1738 punctuates them (*Tum socrus, exspecta, inquit, filia,*); the speech opens with a capital (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: propinquum sic adloquitur: “Fundum agri Elimelechi, consanguinei nostri, venumdat Noemis, ex agro Moabitico reversa.

text: Hac de re mihi visum est, ut te admonerem, ut si eum jure propinquitatis redemturus es, merceris in incolarum senatorumque nostrorum praesentia: sin minus redemturus es, mihi indices, ut dispiciam: neque enim cujusquam magis est redimere quam tuum, secundum quem ego sum.” Tum ille: “Ego redimam,” inquit.
note: Boaz's speech closed at *ego sum.*; the kinsman's answer direct, *Tum ille:* keeping 1738's colon with *inquit* after the words, as the settled *ille: “Quid vīs?” inquit.*; the draft's line break inside the verse goes (1738 runs on) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Et Boozus: “Quum agrum a Noemi emes, habenda tibi est etiam Rutha Moabitis, uxor defuncti, ut defuncti nomen in ejus hereditate suscites.”
note: Boaz's words, direct (no *inquit*: 1738's colon kept) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: At propinquus, “Non possum mihi redimere,” inquit, “ne hereditatem meam corrumpam: redimito tu, quod mei juris est: nam ipse quidem redimere non possum.”
note: the kinsman's words, direct; *inquit* set off by commas, the colon after the speaker a comma, as 3:9 and the settled Judg 6:23 (decision 65) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Erat autem mos olim apud Israelitas, ut qui alteri in jure propinquitatis cedebat, quo res tota confirmaretur, detractum sibi calceum alteri traderet: eratque haec apud Israelitas testificatio.
note: paragraph: the narrator's aside on the custom; the BSB and 1738 both break here; 4:1–12 is 296 words otherwise (decision 52), 146 and 150 after the split (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Et Boozus quum ad omnes, tum ad senatores ita loquitur: “Vos testes estis hodie, me omnes Elimelechi, omnesque Chelionis et Mahalonis facultates emere a Noemi:
note: Boaz's declaration, direct (4:9–10, as the BSB), opened after 1738's colon with a capital; the draft's line break inside the verse goes (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: nec non Rutham Moabitidem, Mahalonis uxorem, mihi in matrimonium conciliare, ut defuncto nomen in sua hereditate suscitem, ne defuncti nomen ex sua consanguinitate patriaque deleatur. Vos hodie testes estis.”
note: Boaz's declaration closed (as the BSB); the draft's line break inside the verse goes (Claude, 2026-11-19)

note: the people's and elders' answer, direct (4:11–12, as the BSB), opened after 1738's colon with a capital; 1738's comma after *sumus* kept; no paragraph for the new speakers (1738 indents here, but no paragraph per speaker, and 4:7 already splits 4:1–12); the draft's line break inside the verse goes (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: sitque domus tua similis domui Pharis, quem ex Thamare Judas sustulit, per progeniem, quam tibi Jova dederit ex hac puella.”
